reason: While hierarchical structures are depicted in the narrative (the Pharaoh's authority over the midwives and his command to all his people), the text does not emphasize or encourage respect for this hierarchy. Rather, the narrative presents the midwives as morally heroic for their act of fear-of-God (יִרְאָה אֱלֹהִים) that leads them to disobey the Pharaoh's command. God explicitly rewards their disobedience: 'And God dealt well with the midwives' (וַיֵּיטֶב אֱלֹהִים לַֽמְיַלְּדֹת). The text demonstrates that loyalty to the divine supersedes loyalty to earthly hierarchy, and the Pharaoh's unjust hierarchical authority is effectively undermined by divine favor granted to those who resist it.
